r4:mesh.summary:
"Save a 3D model" (N6) is built in the two files I own and passes every check on the built-in fields, against base2 and base3, with no console errors. The real src/js/45-export.js never arrived (last looked 23:18, 16 minutes after the first look), so the model export has NOT been run against the real takeSnapshot / sampleSlice. To see the mesher on real distance fields anyway I wrote a private stand-in of that interface (my own 25 lines plus base3's shaders with the uRaw branch added, both under out/r4/mesh/). Through it the Julia set for c = -1, the default Mandelbrot and the default Kleinian each export at 128 cells, the zips unpack with python's zipfile, and the STLs parse back closed. That says nothing about the real module's snapshot freezing or pacing.

What the user gets: a panel with resolution (96 to 512, starts at 128), surface offset (0 to 2 cells, starts 0.5), longest side in mm (100), "Keep only the largest piece" (on), ticks for STL / OBJ / PLY (all on), "Start the model", a progress bar with step, percent, time left and "Cancel", then triangle count, points, size, pieces, file sizes, a warning above two million triangles, "Save the file" and "Discard". The zip holds the chosen files and a readme.txt.

Numbers (base3 build): sphere at 96 cells, offset 0: closed, Euler 2, volume -0.033 %, 68,648 triangles / 34,326 points, points within 0.0016 cells rms of the true sphere. Sphere at defaults: -0.019 %. Torus: closed, Euler 0, -0.089 %. Thin gyroid wall at 192 cells: closed, largest of 121 pieces, 689,200 triangles. Noise field (meets all 256 cases): closed. Field that is zero inside and reads 1.6x long outside (the Kleinian situation): closed, volume -0.43 %. Longest pause of the page's timers during a job 28 to 40 ms; cancel in 11 ms. Through the stand-in: Julia 27,232 triangles, 1 piece, 0.5 s; Mandelbrot 86,360 triangles, largest of 156 pieces; Kleinian 93,224 triangles, 1 piece; all closed in the mesh and in the STL read back.

Two things the tests caught and I fixed: (1) a first triangle table (fan fill) failed the closed test on noise, because a fill line could lie in a cube face shared with the neighbour; (2) "largest piece" renumbered points in an order that overwrote points still to be moved, which only showed when the STL was welded by position.

Decisions beyond the spec, all stated in the readme or notes: the model is clipped by the drawing radius and by the cut plane when the solid is cut open (it matches the picture); coordinates are mm, standing on z = 0, centred on the z-axis; the OBJ is written y-up so it stands like the STL and PLY after Blender's or Rhino's usual OBJ turn; file colours are display values (linear to the power 1/2.2); jobs stop with a plain message above 15 million triangles or about 1.4 GB of files. The triangle table was generated and checked by a script rather than typed from memory (same numbering and face rule as the standard table; the edge table is the standard one).

needs_from_others: render-export (src/js/45-export.js, src/js/40-render.js): sampleSlice must accept any N from 8 to 513, not only the listed resolutions. The model grid uses cells + 1 samples a side (97, 129, 193, 257, 385, 513) and the search uses about 100 small calls (N between 8 and 96) with a different centre and side per pass. Calls come one at a time; takeSnapshot() is called inside the click handler and releaseSnapshot(snap) in a finally. A null result ends the job with 'The picture could not be read just now...'.

render-export / shaders: the alpha written with uRaw on must be the plain de() value (positive outside, zero or negative inside) with the cut plane ignored: 46-mesh.js applies the cut (max(d, z - cut)) and the drawing radius (max(d, |p| - bound)) itself from S as it is at the click. An exact 0 is read as 'nothing known inside' (the Kleinian pearls); any other inside value is used as a distance.

risks: The whole real path rests on an interface I could only exercise through my own stand-in. If the real sampleSlice differs from CONTRACT4 in any detail (row order, alpha meaning, odd N), the model will be wrong until that is found; rerun 'run_tests.py real' as soon as 45-export.js is in.

Time per job with the real module is unknown: the job makes roughly 100 small sampleSlice calls to find the solid and then cells + 1 large ones. With my synchronous stand-in a 128-cell job took 0.5 s; a paced implementation will be slower, and at 128 cells the search could be about half the total.

The host's size limit for saveFile is unknown. The default (128 cells, three formats) gave zips of 3 to about 10 MB on the real pictures; 384 cells gave 318 MB on a test field. A refused save shows the core's sentence and keeps the model for another try.
The box found by the search is 5 to 8 percent loose on each side, so the solid spans about 85 to 90 percent of the chosen cell count. The saved size is still exact.

'Largest piece' is judged by triangle count: a solid made of two equal halves loses one of them, and inner hollows are dropped. The default Mandelbrot of base3 kept the largest of 156 pieces. The user can untick the box.

Where the field is exactly 0 inside and reads long outside, points are placed to about a third of a cell (0.11 cells rms on the test field). The Kleinian pearls looked smooth in the test picture, but I judged it from my own small rasteriser, not from Blender.

At 128 cells the model is visibly coarser than the on-screen picture (see real-mandel-picture.png beside real-mandel-mesh.png). I kept 128 as the starting value for speed and file size; 192 or 256 gives a model closer to the picture.

The triangle table is generated, not the textbook table byte for byte: same numbering, same face rule and the standard edge table, but some cases are split into triangles along different lines. It is checked exhaustively and by closed-surface tests.

Memory: a job is stopped above 15 million triangles or about 1.4 GB of files, but a browser with little memory could fail earlier; that case shows 'The model could not be built... Try a lower resolution' and logs the error to the console.
